clue.text: See 18
Very hot situation: cubicle door finally blown

indicators.note: something blown apart is scattered, so these letters are rearranged
finally points to the closing letter of door

parts.note: its last letter is R

explanation.surface: A bathroom cubicle door is blasted off in a scene of great heat and pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R, the last letter of door; 'blown' rearranges CUBICLE plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucible is figuratively a severe test or trial under intense pressure, as well as a vessel for melting metal.

clue.text: See 8
Far right in Texas involved in notorious trial town with a new representative

indicators.note: the S is taken into the middle of the town's name

parts.note: Salem, Massachusetts, site of the 1692 witch trials

parts.note: its last letter is S

explanation.surface: A political tale of the far right in Texas getting tangled up in a famous trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far right in Texas' is S, the last letter; 'involved in' puts it inside SALEM, the witch-trial town, before A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesman is a sales representative, someone employed to sell a company's goods.

clue.text: Be protected by a plant, a tufty one

indicators.note: being protected means being enclosed, so BE goes within the plant

parts.note: the iris is a familiar garden plant

explanation.surface: An instruction to shelter under a plant with tufts.

explanation.definitionFit: Iberis is the genus name of candytuft, a garden plant named for its tufted clusters of flowers.

clue.text: Scientist from Syracuse building bridges across island and sea

indicators.note: the bridges stretch across, spanning the other letters inside them

I is the map abbreviation for island
MED is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: An engineer from Syracuse builds bridges over an island and the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' is only a link here, though it reads as part of the bridging picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek mathematician and inventor lived and died in Syracuse, Sicily, in the third century BC.

clue.text: Daisy, perhaps, works on US TV series

parts.note: a mill is a factory, a works
ER is the American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: Someone called Daisy works on an American television show.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Miller is the title heroine of a Henry James novella; 'perhaps' marks her as one example of someone with this surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisy Miller, Henry James's young American heroine, is an example of a person with this surname.

clue.text: Broadcast about hospital department deputy initially being put away

indicators.note: the sown letters go around the department and the initial

ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of deputy

parts.note: its first letter is D

explanation.surface: A broadcast about a deputy from a hospital department being locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' is not a radio programme but the past participle of scattering seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sent down is British slang for being jailed, just as 'put away' means imprisoned.

clue.text: Sign of very independent move to crush queen

indicators.note: the letters before the queen and after squeeze her between them

parts.note: go means move
R for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A chess-like picture of an independent move to crush the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to crush' puts R (regina, queen) inside V, I and GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, the Virgin.

clue.text: Vegetable served up by inn outside Northern Ireland retreat

explanation.walkthrough: The inn is the French word, which English borrows for a country inn or restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine is the British name for the eggplant, a purple vegetable.

clue.text: Source of story of Egyptian god scam (true version)

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
a con is a scam

indicators.note: a version of a word is a different form of it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tale about an Egyptian god turns out to be a scam, with the true version in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: RA and CON are followed by TEUR, the rearrangement of TRUE that 'version' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes, so stories come from them.

clue.text: Composer about to back away from gun carrier?

indicators.note: the turned letters go away from the gun carrier, leaving the rest

explanation.walkthrough: RE (about) is turned by 'to back' into ER, which goes 'away from' HOLSTER.

clue.text: Freely confess: 'Ridiculous bonus over short time'

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
M, the short form of minute, a brief time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ridiculous' rearranges BONUS into UNBOS, followed by O for over and M for minute.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbosom is an old verb meaning to disclose one's feelings or secrets openly.

clue.text: Withdraw tender without any prompting?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to undo a bid, taking back an offer

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful coinage, un- plus bid; the question mark flags that it is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means uninvited or unasked, and read as un- plus bid it suggests retracting an offer.

clue.text: English audacity, with opponents getting laundered cash

parts.note: sass is cheeky audacity
East and North are opponents at the bridge table

indicators.note: laundered money is washed around, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A story of English cheek as rivals clean dirty money.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play East-West, so E and N are opponents; 'laundered' rearranges CASH to ACHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is a Scottish, often derogatory, term for English people.

clue.text: Smith, the singer, has song for a biblical region

parts.note: Sam Smith is the English pop singer
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: The singer Sam Smith performs a song about a place in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' joins SAM to ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Samaria was the ancient region of Israel, home of the Good Samaritan in the Gospels.

clue.text: When embracing Latin American hero is painful

Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.walkthrough: 'When' gives AS through its use in phrases like 'as I left'.

clue.text: Lay hands on book of not so great size

parts.note: less means of smaller size or amount

explanation.surface: Grabbing a book that is on the small side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay hands on' looks like grabbing, but it is the laying on of hands in a blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests bless people by laying hands on them, a gesture of consecration.

clue.text: Though possibly Adam, right? Under no circumstances

parts.note: Adam was not Eve, though he might be described that way

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking whether it could be Adam, and the emphatic reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam is 'not Eve'; add R for right to make NOT EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'not ever' means never, in no situation at all.

clue.text: If paint is this, it produces discomfort

definitions.text: If paint is this, it produces discomfort

parts.words: If paint is this, it produces discomfort
parts.note: the word is read as lacking T, a letter for time; paint without that letter is a word for discomfort

explanation.walkthrough: T is the abbreviation for time; 'paint' without its T is 'pain', the discomfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, the word means without T, and removing T from paint leaves an ache.

clue.text: Departure from idea thrills

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Breaking away from an idea that excites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to letters inside 'idea thrills'.
explanation.definitionFit: Departure is a euphemism for dying, as in 'the departed'.

clue.text: One lot of detectives having shower, possibly cause of bad atmosphere

parts.note: a means one
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
rain falls in a shower

explanation.surface: A police squad all having a shower creates a tense atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad atmosphere' looks like a tense mood but is literal air pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollutants in the air form acidic precipitation, which damages forests and buildings.

clue.text: Laid-back court accepts English as a form of language

back means the word is read in reverse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid-back' reads as relaxed but splits into a word and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional variety of a language with its own words and grammar.

clue.text: Hit film comedy, Garfunkel, followed by second half of biblical epic

explanation.walkthrough: 'second half of' keeps HUR from BEN-HUR.

clue.text: Handy device prescribed by the doctor?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hand-held touchscreen computer

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a portable touchscreen computer and a pressed pill of medicine.

clue.text: Mavericks getting female to keep in good shape?

clue.text: Cherished origins of royal and ancient tourist destination

indicators.note: origins are starting points, the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: A beloved ancient royal site that draws tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins of' takes R and A from 'royal' and 'ancient'.
explanation.definitionFit: Petra is the rock-cut ancient city in Jordan, one of the world's most visited sites.

clue.text: Way to hit hard

parts.note: pat means a light hit
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A way of hitting something hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link joining the definition to PAT and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a route or track, a way from one place to another.

clue.text: Two-sided legislation about a rate change

indicators.note: change means the letters are altered in order

explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges A RATE to LATERA; 'about' puts BILL around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral means involving or affecting two sides or parties, as in a treaty.

clue.text: Small shark's peak energy

parts.note: the top is the peak
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A small shark is at its peak of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The tope is a small European shark, also known as the school shark.

clue.text: Hull element turns up for Peak District town

clue.text: Literary heroine, awfully gung-ho on the inside, but lacking good resilience
